title: RSA Paper
summary: An RSA-encrypted message uses a dangerously small modulus. Factor it and decrypt.
briefing:
An encrypted message was intercepted from a NebulaCorp internal relay. The encryption uses textbook RSA — each byte of the plaintext is encrypted independently as c = m^e mod n, with no padding.

The modulus n is suspiciously small. If you can factor it into its two prime components p and q, you can compute the private exponent d and decrypt the message.

Steps:
1. Factor n into primes p × q (hint: both primes are under 110,000)
2. Compute φ(n) = (p−1)(q−1)
3. Compute d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n) (modular inverse)
4. For each ciphertext integer c, compute m = c^d mod n
5. Convert each m to its ASCII character

The decrypted message is the flag. Submit it exactly as it appears.
objectives: Factor the modulus n by trial division

hints.title: Factoring approach
hints.text: Try dividing n by every odd number from 3 up to sqrt(n). With both primes under 110,000, trial division finishes in milliseconds. In Python: for i in range(3, 110000, 2): if n % i == 0: print(i, n//i); break

hints.title: Decryption in Python
hints.text: Use pow(c, d, n) for modular exponentiation. chr(pow(c, d, n)) gives the ASCII character. Apply to each line of ciphertext.

artifacts.description: Intercepted RSA-encrypted transmission with public key parameters.
